source.title: Suppressing Mislabeled Data via Grouping and Self-attention
source.authors: Xiao-Jiang Peng; Kai Wang; Zhaoyang Zeng; Qing Li; Jianfei Yang; Y. Qiao

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests training with noisy labels, including a synthetic sweep from 20% to 100% noise, but does not test completely random labels, unstructured inputs, or the original claim's training recipe. Its results refine the noise-generalization claim in a distinct AFM method and setting.
record.gate_note: The study's own noisy-label training results and AFM attention-weight visualizations bear on V4 and V6. References to Rolnick et al. and Arpit et al. are prior work, not this study's results. Table 3–6 and Figure 3–5 report AFM or mixup comparisons, but do not directly measure the claim versions and are omitted as rows. Figure 6 visualizes attention weights, but gives no numeric measurement of learning real-label patterns before noisy-label memorization.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates mitigation of real-world label noise, without measuring memorization or its learning dynamics. Figure 4 varies dataset size, not label-noise fraction; Figure 6 shows learned attention weights, not when clean and noisy labels are fitted. No own result tests V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that AFM uses grouping and self-attention to suppress mislabeled samples and achieves strong results on Food101N and Clothing1M without requiring an extra clean subset.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces an attentive feature-mixup training block on real-world noisy datasets; uses a pretrained ResNet50 and specified SGD setup, rather than the original random-label memorization intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Figure 4 varies synthetic Food101N dataset size/noise ratio; the text says AFM's gains from 40% to 100% data exceed those at 20%.

fits_no_version.finding: AFM improves baseline test accuracy across randomly reduced Food101N subsets, with larger gains at 40%–100% data than at 20%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attentive Feature Mixup improves generalization on smaller subsets of a real-world noisy-label dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 6 qualitatively shows lower AFM attention weights for noisy members of clean/noisy pairs; removing projection loses this discrimination.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The trained AFM attention module can downweight mislabeled samples relative to clean samples within mixed pairs.

record.problems: For the potentially relevant noise sweep, the results are only plotted, without values or uncertainty in the text. It reports test accuracy rather than training error and does not state the exact synthetic label-corruption procedure. The study evaluates AFM, not unchanged standard training on completely random labels.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 1–6 and Figures 3–5 report AFM and comparator benchmark or ablation results, not the claim's versions measuring random-label fitting, fit time, unstructured inputs, regularization on random labels, or memorization order. Figure 6 attention-weight visualizations do not measure V6's temporal learning-order claim.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to near-zero training error under unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, with chance test performance.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence changes with corruption fraction. Table 1 instead compares AFM and baseline runtime on the same noisy dataset.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across a controlled label-corruption sweep. Figure 4 varies sample count only.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Temporal order of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noise. Attention-weight visualizations do not measure fitting order.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the proposed V4 limits_scope verdict: missing training-error measurements are untested components, not evidence of a limitation. The record's claimed synthetic noise sweep is a misreading of the dataset-size experiment.

versions.untested_parts: No fully random labeling experiment or test error at chance; no test of whether unchanged standard training fits such labels.
No training-time comparison for fitting random versus true labels or convergence-time sweep by corrupted-label fraction.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.
The experiment varies synthetic label-noise ratio on Food101N, but only Figure 4 reports it; the text does not specify the exact corruption procedure, training error, or all-noisy condition.
No experiment removes or varies weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation on random labels.
Figure 6 describes clean/noisy sample attention weights for pairs, but does not measure temporal order of fitting real patterns versus noisy labels.

rows.subject: ResNet50 (baseline)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Food101N with AFM under varied synthetic dataset sizes/noise ratios; clean Food-101 test accuracy reported.
rows.note: Baseline series in Figure 4; exact values unavailable in text. This is the non-AFM comparator in the AFM data-size/noise-ratio experiment.
rows.check: Figure 4 measures baseline test accuracy across dataset sizes, not corruption rates. Remove 'with AFM' from the baseline operation description. The plotted percentages are retained data fractions; 100% means the full Food101N dataset, not fully random labels. This method-comparison series does not measure V4.

rows.subject: AFM (Ours)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Food101N with Attentive Feature Mixup under varied synthetic dataset sizes/noise ratios; clean Food-101 test accuracy reported.
rows.note: AFM series in Figure 4; exact values unavailable in text. The stated result says AFM consistently improves the baseline, but the figure's accuracy is not numerically described.
rows.check: Figure 4 evaluates AFM test accuracy across dataset sizes, not corruption rates. It reports neither training fit nor degradation as label corruption increases. This method-performance series should not be a claim-result row. The extraction also incorrectly says numerical annotations are unavailable: the supplied figure text includes accuracy values.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: AFM on synthetic Food101N subsets at 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100% of data
reader_labels.reason: AFM consistently improves baseline test accuracy, but the text does not report training error or establish perfect training fit as noise rises; Figure 4's test values are figure-only (R1–R2).
